page.layout: Two-column printed page? No: one page of text in a single column, with marginal notes in the left margin ("Quaestio." beside the line "Nulli ne ergo", "Clementia." beside "terlucentia"). Running head at top right, page number at top left. A chapter number and title sit centred in the text, with a Greek passage in the middle of the column.

main_text.p: Galliarum, plura in Afiatico regno exempla: quæ bre- vitatis studio non scrutor.

Quaestio.Nulli ne ergo principi (peculatores, delatores, accu- fatores fovendi? Temporum neceffitas, ut multa ad quæ connivendum, ita & eahominum portenta alii-quando admittit. Quibus quatenus aures præben- dæ, Mæcenas Augustum, 52 libro Dionis, edocet.
Non omnia ftatim quæ ab his referun- tur, credenda: fed diligens adhibenda confideratio eft.

Permultienim velodio aliorum, vel facultatum eo- rum appetentia, velin aliorum gratiam, vel irati ob- poftulatam ab aliis, ac non acceptam, pecuniam; eos novarum rerum crimine, aut alicujus contra impera- torem abfurde concepti aut dicti facinoris, evertunt. Ideo non temere animus iis eft advertendus, fed o- mnia accurate indaganda. Quæ indagatio quibus artibus apte fieri poffit, nos in Arcanis regnorum re- clufimus.
main_text.head: De fuo clementia, non dealieno largitur.
main_text.p: Quemadmodum liberalitas non eft, quæ fundum alienum exhaurit; ita clementiæ nomen non mere- tur, quæ aliorum injuriis condonandis largum finum effundit. Tiberius in fuo dolore largæ, in alieno aftri- ctæ lenitudinis exempla, multis fævitiæ exemplis in- Clementia.terlucentia, præbuit. 1. C. Cominium equitem Romanum probrofi in fe carminis convictum, Cafar precibus fratris qui fenator erat, concessit. page.notes: Greek passages in the middle of the column (about nine lines) and the Greek word before "Non omnia" are not legible enough to copy letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The Greek is not transliterated. The left margin notes are "Quaestio." and "Clementia.". The Latin is copied from the scan; doubtful words are not marked here, but "fovendi?" is a possible misreading. The page is set in roman type with Greek inserted.
